metaDescription: Alexander sits in core McKenzie County Bakken territory near Watford City. See what a family mineral interest here typically looks like today.
heroLead: Alexander is a small McKenzie County town sitting right inside some of the most heavily drilled ground in the entire Bakken.
intro: A short drive from Watford City, Alexander sits in core McKenzie County, where dense horizontal drilling into the Bakken and Three Forks has run for well over a decade. Families who homesteaded or ranched near Alexander often kept minerals through the leaner years before the shale boom, and today those same tracts can sit inside busy, multi-well spacing units. If you inherited an interest tied to Alexander and haven't looked at it recently, it's worth checking against current production records rather than assuming nothing has changed.

sections.heading: Why Alexander Sits in the Thick of Bakken Activity
paragraphs: McKenzie County holds some of the densest well spacing in the entire Williston Basin, and acreage around Alexander has seen extensive horizontal development targeting both the Bakken and the underlying Three Forks bench. A tract here is far more likely to sit inside an active or historically productive unit than one in a flank county to the north or south.

sections.heading: What Ownership Near Alexander Usually Looks Like
paragraphs: Many mineral interests here trace to ranch and farm families who homesteaded McKenzie County in the early 1900s, with fractions now split among heirs who may live anywhere from Bismarck to the East Coast. Confirming your exact share starts with your legal description and the McKenzie County Recorder's chain of title, not with family recollection alone.

sections.heading: What to Do Before Accepting Any Offer
paragraphs: Given how much production density this part of McKenzie County carries, we always recommend pulling a current division order and well list before weighing any offer on an Alexander-area interest, since a single legal description here can be tied to more value, or more complexity, than a quick look suggests. That review costs you nothing and gives you a real basis for comparison.

faqs.question: Is Alexander, ND inside core Bakken drilling territory?
faqs.answer: Yes, Alexander sits within McKenzie County's core Bakken and Three Forks trend, one of the most heavily developed parts of the basin.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my Alexander-area interest is currently leased?
faqs.answer: Check your legal description against North Dakota Industrial Commission spacing and well records, or send it to us and we'll look it up at no cost.

faqs.question: Why did my family's Alexander mineral interest sit quiet for so long before producing?
faqs.answer: Many McKenzie County tracts were held for decades before horizontal drilling technology made them economical to develop starting in the mid-2000s, which is a common pattern across this part of the county.

faqs.question: Will selling my Alexander mineral interest affect future wells drilled on my tract?
faqs.answer: Once a sale closes, future production from that interest belongs to the buyer, which is exactly why reviewing current and likely future activity on your specific tract matters before you decide.
